1.title: Ports, Protocols and Services
1.text: Welcome to Module four: Ports, Protocols and Services. It covers the exam area one point zero Networking Concepts. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. one point four Explain common networking ports, protocols, services and traffic types: the port list. I P types (I C M P, T C P, U D P, G R E, I P sec with A H, E S P and I K E). Traffic types (unicast, multicast, anycast, broadcast). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one point zero Networking Concepts (twenty-three percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: The port list to memorize
1.text: The port list to memorize. F T P (File Transfer Protocol). Port: twenty or twenty-one. Notes: Clear text; twenty-one control, twenty data. S F T P (Secure F T P). Port: twenty-two. Notes: Runs over S S H. S S H (Secure Shell). Port: twenty-two. Notes: Encrypted remote administration. Telnet. Port: twenty-three. Notes: Clear text remote login (avoid). S M T P. Port: twenty-five. Notes: Sends mail between servers. D N S. Port: fifty-three. Notes: Names to addresses, U D P and T C P. D H C P. Port: sixty-seven or sixty-eight. Notes: sixty-seven server, sixty-eight client, U D P. T F T P. Port: sixty-nine. Notes: Simple, unauthenticated file transfer, U D P. H T T P. Port: eighty. Notes: Web, clear text.

1.title: The port list to memorize, continued
1.text: The port list to memorize. N T P. Port: one hundred twenty-three. Notes: Time, U D P. S N M P. Port: one hundred sixty-one or one hundred sixty-two. Notes: one hundred sixty-one queries, one hundred sixty-two traps. L D A P (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol). Port: three hundred eighty-nine. Notes: Directory access. H T T P S. Port: four hundred forty-three. Notes: Web over T L S. S M B (Server Message Block). Port: four hundred forty-five. Notes: Windows file sharing. Syslog. Port: five hundred fourteen. Notes: Log messages, U D P. S M T P S. Port: five hundred eighty-seven. Notes: Secure mail submission. L D A P S. Port: six hundred thirty-six. Notes: L D A P over S S L or T L S. sequel Server. Port: one thousand four hundred thirty-three. Notes: Microsoft sequel database. R D P. Port: three thousand three hundred eighty-nine. Notes: Remote Desktop. S I P. Port: five thousand sixty or five thousand sixty-one. Notes: Voice signaling; five thousand sixty-one is encrypted.

1.title: The port list to memorize, continued
1.text: The port list to memorize. The figure shows this: Well-known ports grouped by purpose. Exam tip: Secure versions use different ports: S S H twenty-two (not Telnet twenty-three), H T T P S four hundred forty-three (not H T T P eighty), L D A P S six hundred thirty-six (not L D A P three hundred eighty-nine). S S H, S F T P share port twenty-two.

1.title: IP types
1.text: I P types. I C M P. Error and diagnostic messages (ping, traceroute); no ports. T C P. Reliable, connection-oriented: handshake, acknowledgements, retransmission, ordering. U D P. Fast, connectionless, no guarantee (voice, D N S, streaming). G R E (Generic Routing Encapsulation). Tunnels other protocols inside I P. I P sec. Secures I P traffic: A H (Authentication Header: integrity and authentication, no encryption), E S P (Encapsulating Security Payload: encryption plus integrity), I K E (Internet Key Exchange: negotiates keys and security associations). Exam tip: T C P equals reliable and slower; U D P equals fast and unreliable. E S P encrypts; A H does not.

1.title: Traffic types
1.text: Traffic types. Unicast. One sender to one receiver. Multicast. One sender to a group that joined. Anycast. One sender to the nearest of several receivers sharing an address. Broadcast. One sender to every device on the local network. IPv six has no broadcast; it uses multicast. Exam tip: Know the secure pairs: H T T P eighty and H T T P S four hundred forty-three, L D A P three hundred eighty-nine and L D A P S six hundred thirty-six, S M T P twenty-five and S M T P S five hundred eighty-seven, Telnet twenty-three and S S H twenty-two.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. An administrator needs an encrypted remote command line to a switch. Which protocol and port fit? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: S S H on port twenty-two. S S H provides encrypted remote administration on port twenty-two.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A web server must allow secure browsing. Which port should the firewall allow? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: four hundred forty-three. H T T P S uses port four hundred forty-three.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which protocol uses ports one hundred sixty-one and one hundred sixty-two? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: S N M P. S N M P uses one hundred sixty-one for queries and one hundred sixty-two for traps.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which I P sec component provides encryption of the payload? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: E S P. E S P encrypts; A H only authenticates.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Traffic is delivered to the closest of several servers that share one I P address. Which traffic type is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Anycast. Anycast delivers to the nearest member.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which transport protocol is best for real-time voice where speed matters more than retransmission? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: U D P. U D P is fast and connectionless.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which port does D N S use? Answer: fifty-three. Question two. Which ports does D H C P use? Answer: sixty-seven (server) and sixty-eight (client). Question three. Which port does R D P use? Answer: three thousand three hundred eighty-nine.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does I K E do? Answer: Negotiates keys and security associations for I P sec. Question five. Is there broadcast in IPv six? Answer: No, IPv six uses multicast. Question six. Which protocol uses port three hundred eighty-nine, and which secure version uses six hundred thirty-six? Answer: L D A P (three hundred eighty-nine) and L D A P S (six hundred thirty-six).

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Remote: S S H twenty-two, Telnet twenty-three, R D P three thousand three hundred eighty-nine. Web and mail: H T T P eighty, H T T P S four hundred forty-three, S M T P twenty-five, S M T P S five hundred eighty-seven. Infrastructure: D N S fifty-three, D H C P sixty-seven or sixty-eight, N T P one hundred twenty-three, S N M P one hundred sixty-one or one hundred sixty-two, Syslog five hundred fourteen, T F T P sixty-nine. Files and directories: F T P twenty or twenty-one, S F T P twenty-two, S M B four hundred forty-five, L D A P three hundred eighty-nine, L D A P S six hundred thirty-six. Traffic: unicast, multicast, anycast, broadcast. I P sec: A H (no encryption), E S P (encrypts), I K E (keys).
